note: v1, SO FAR: THE WHOLE SHAPE STANDING (the song I wanted to make; 4:42, 130 BPM, F). THE IDEA: take a number; halve it if it is even, treble it and add one if it is odd; go on until you reach one. Every number anyone has tried gets there and nobody has proved every number must. The song tries the first sixteen, in order, and plays each walk in full, end to end; nothing is repeated or cut to fit. A NUMBER IS THREE THINGS: its length (n sixteenths); its note (the n-th harmonic of the low F: 3 is C, 5 A, 7 E-flat, 9 G, 11 B, 13 D-flat), so a halving falls an octave in half the time; and its riff (its odd part written in twos, a stroke for a one and a rest for a nought, said round and round: 40, 20, 10, 5 is one phrase in half notes, quarters, eighths, sixteenths). Every walk ends alike: sixteen, eight, four, two, one, a ball coming to rest on F. The kit is outside the rule and keeps common time throughout. LISTEN FOR: 0:17.4, seven (288 sixteenths, eighteen bars exactly), where the second guitar joins; 2:06.7-2:28.2, twelve and thirteen on the ondes and the bass alone over a ride and a rim; 2:28.2, fourteen: seven said at half speed, then seven's whole walk again; 3:03.0, fifteen, eighty seconds long: it climbs to 160 (ten bars on one chord at 3:43) and the ondes, which plays each number at its true height, is out of sight from 3:43 to 4:11 and comes back from the top at 40; 4:26.7, the wheel four, two, one (one is not an end), fifteen turns of seven sixteenths, which is what brings it back to a bar line. THE BAND: two ct-twin guitars, ct-bass, ct-kit, and the library ondes Martenot as the lead. THE DRAW'S ROUND TYPE WAS instrument; on an empty slot the first round is the song, and the one instrument I set by measurement is the lead: 2.5 dB off each note per octave over middle C (a sine stood 2.5 dB under the band up high and 8.8 down low), its diffuser halved and 3 dB off at 350 Hz (it held 45% of 250-500 Hz; now 24%). MEASURED (seeds 0/11): 87.033 / 85.134; the first bare draft read 79.62 / 80.192. Against the eleven records 250-500 Hz reads 2.5 to 2.9 dB over in the long walks (4.2 in the opening on one guitar); everything else within 2.4 dB except 8-16 kHz in the climb (+3.5). The loud walks all sit within 1 dB of each other (-12.0 to -13.2 K); twelve and thirteen are 4 dB under. No card: nothing here needs his ear to go on. WHICH OF HIS RULES I TOOK AS BINDING: all of direction.rules; no words, so the vocal rules do not arise. Not heard by me.
next: It is bare, and anyone may build on it. In order of what I would do: (1) DYNAMICS: the loud walks are one level and one texture (variety is the weak term, 64-70): give nine, eleven and fifteen each a different kit feel and guitar register; fifteen's climb (3:03-3:43) should grow, and 160 should be the biggest thing in the song. (2) The opening seventeen seconds (one to six) are one guitar and a kick at full level: a real entrance. (3) The ondes: whether out of sight should be silence (as now) or something else is an ear's call; TOP in the generator is the top of the ribbon, TILT its level slope, --lead-gain its fader. (4) The second guitar's small phrase under 40, 80 and 160 could be a different sound. (5) 250-500 Hz is still 2.5-2.9 over: the guitars hold 30% of it (the album's 380 Hz cut is not on them here). Do not cut or repeat a walk to make the form tidier: that each takes as long as it takes is the song. --form prints where each walk starts.

note:
v2, THE SUMMIT HAS ITS FALL INSIDE IT (chirper-three; section round, windows 8 and 9; the change is 3:43.2–4:10.9, the top of the fifteenth walk and its first step down). v1's note asked that 160 be the biggest thing in the song. Measured, it was the smallest of the loud stretches: ten bars on one chord, the left guitar striking twice and ringing for half of it, 1.9 dB under the long walks in the finished file. LISTEN FOR 3:43.2, the top: four guitars now, the new pair on the low A, a crash, the hands on the china; under the chord the bass no longer holds, it moves (A, a short F, A, every two and a half beats). 4:01.6, 80: the left guitar comes down to what the new pair is already playing. 4:10.9, 40: the new pair stops and the whole band is on the riff the bass has had since the top; the ondes comes back there as before.
THE IDEA: 160 is not one number. It is 80 doubled and 40 doubled twice, down to five: ONE phrase (stroke, rest, stroke) in six sizes, and from the top the walk does nothing but go down through them. v1 played two of the sizes at the top (the number's own, two bars a place, on the left guitar; the smallest, in sixteenths, on the right guitar and the kick). Now the sizes between are heard, each on what will have it next: TWO MORE GUITARS (the album's wall rig, new tracks wall-left and wall-right) say eighty's phrase, a bar a place, a storey under the number (A1, E2, A2); the BASS says forty's, half a bar a place, exactly as it plays it at 40. So at the top every chord of the next thirty seconds is already going, and the fall takes a storey off at a time. The kit's hands stay in common time, as v1 rules; the foot, which is in the rule, is lifted on the new pair's four chords that it already played softly.
WHAT CHANGED: 18 notes on the two new tracks; the bass's six notes in 160 and 80 become eighteen; four kick strokes go from 0.78 to 0.95; the ride's 40 quarters in 160 are the china and one crash is added at 3:43.2. No walk is cut, repeated or moved, and no guitar, ondes or snare note changed.
WHAT I MEASURED (raw window on seed 0, then finished files on seeds 0 and 11). FIRST BENCH, not kept: the new pair at the album's setting (-3.5 dB, 3 dB off at 380 Hz) lifted 160 by 1.9 dB raw but put 3.3 dB into 250-500 Hz, where v1's note already reads the song 2.5 to 2.9 over the records. KEPT: the pair at -1 dB with 6 dB off at 380 Hz. Finished, 160 reads -13.89 -> -11.55 and -13.84 -> -11.63 dB (K; +2.3 and +2.2), and 80 reads -13.07 -> -11.52 and -11.50 (+1.6). THAT MAKES 160 LEVEL WITH THE LOUDEST STRETCH OF THE SONG, NOT OVER IT: the start of the fifteenth walk reads -11.54 and -11.64, the other long walks -12.0. It is the biggest by what is in it (four guitars, the low A, the china), and by half a decibel over seven, nine, eleven and fourteen. COST, benched raw at -2 dB on the pair: 160 carries 1.8 dB more of its level at 250-500 Hz than the walks either side (2.8 more in 80), and the china puts +4.5 dB at 8-16 kHz for those ten bars. Everything outside 3:43.2–4:10.9 is unchanged on both seeds (-66.5 dB residual or lower, 0.006 dB or less); the first half second of 40 differs by -44 dB (the pair's last chord ringing out). Loudness target -9.81 (was -10): at -10 every other bar came out 0.17 to 0.18 dB quieter.
SCORES 0/11: 87.033/85.134 -> 86.685/85.590 (-0.35, +0.46): kept on judgment. Variety rises on both seeds (70.4 -> 71.7, 64.6 -> 65.9). Structure falls on seed 0 (68.4 -> 65.3) and rises on seed 11 (64.0 -> 65.3): the scorer counts 21 sections where it wants at most 19, and on one of its seven cuts the count moved by one. -9.8 LUFS, -1.29 dBTP.
WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether four guitars on one chord for ten bars read as a summit or as a wall with the detail gone; whether the bass's moving line is heard under them; whether the low A1 chords are weight or mud.

If the top is mud, put the pair at the left guitar's own octave (field four = 0) before lowering it; if the pair buries the left guitar's two strokes, -3 in field two. Re-fit SUMMIT_LOUDNESS after any change (render once, read the gain of an untouched minute against v1, move the target by it). STILL TO DO, from v1's list: 160 is level with the loudest stretch, not over it, and the way to make it the biggest is to bring the CLIMB up to it (15 to 53, 3:03–3:43, is flat, and 106 and 53 are 1 dB under the walk's first bars) and to give nine, eleven and fourteen their own levels, not to push the top into the limiter. The sizes not yet heard at the top are 20 and 10 (a quarter and an eighth a place): a second voice for them would finish the tower, and the ondes, which is out of sight there, is the obvious one if it may play below its true height. The kit's hands stay outside the rule (v1): do not put them on the phrase. 250-500 Hz is still over on the whole song: the first pair has no cut at 380 Hz. Do not cut or repeat a walk.
